deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This belongs to the 1983 'Teichmüller-Lego' work on the modular orbifold M_{0,4}/S_4, the moduli of 4 unordered points I = {a,b,c,d} on P^1. It is the same object as M_{1,1}, the modular curve with ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1 and ρσ = l (parabolic), as written on p.19. Grothendieck uses three kinds of distinguished 'base points', listed on p.17:
(i) tetrahedral structures: the 4 points are the vertices of a regular tetrahedron inscribed in the sphere. This is the equianharmonic cross-ratio, the orbifold point of order 3. There are 2 such structures, one for each orientation of I.
(ii) 'carré' (square) structures: the 4 points are the vertices of a square on a great circle. This is the harmonic cross-ratio, the orbifold point of order 2. There are 3, one for each partition of I into two pairs (Q_0, Q_1, Q_∞ on p.19).
(iii) 'pantalonesque' structures: stable degenerations, i.e. the cusp, a pants decomposition or tangential base point at infinity.
He also lists elementary paths between these, to be visualised conformally (as deformations of point configurations) and combinatorially (as maps, i.e. 'cartes', on the sphere).

This page.
1. Top figure, 'passage du carré [transcribed 'cube'] aux deux tétraèdres'. The four black points sit on the equator in square position. Arrows on meridians (red for one choice, green for the other) show alternate vertices moving up and the other two moving down. One choice reaches one regular tetrahedron, the other reaches the opposite one. The two tetrahedra together form the vertices of a cube. So each square base point is joined by elementary paths to both tetrahedral base points, i.e. both orientations. This is the conformal picture of the path σ-point → ρ-point.
2. Right margin. To see the passage from the square to the pantalonesque structures, one must use the full barycentric subdivision of the square map: 4 vertices, 4 edges forming the equator, 2 hemispherical faces. The degenerations that collide two adjacent vertices correspond to edge midpoints; the motions toward the tetrahedra correspond to the face centres.
3. General principle, middle left. In both 'special' non-degenerate cases (square, tetrahedron), all adjacent base-point positions are 'contained' in the barycentric subdivision of the corresponding map. That is, the neighbours of a base point in the Lego graph are read off from the cells of the barycentric subdivision.
4. Coloured tetrahedron figure. The tetrahedral map has 4 vertices, 6 edges and 4 faces; its barycentric subdivision (green) has 14 vertices and 24 triangles. It also contains the barycentric subdivisions of the three associated square maps (one shown in red dotted lines).
- Concretely, the square a-b-c-d uses 4 of the 6 edges and omits the opposite pair ac, bd.
- The two face centres of the square map become the midpoints of ac and bd.
- A spoke from a face centre to a, c is an edge of the tetrahedral subdivision. A spoke to b, d, or to a midpoint of the square's edges, is a 2-edge path through a tetrahedral face centre.
So the square subdivision (10 vertices, 24 edges, 16 triangles) embeds as a topological subdivision, not a subcomplex.
5. Bottom pencil sphere: an unfinished sketch of points on a sphere with equator and meridians, probably a further configuration (square plus poles, or the octahedral view).

Purpose: to build an explicit combinatorial model (the Lego) of the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4}/S_4, based at the symmetric points and at infinity. It feeds the group-theoretic picture on p.19, with T_{0,4}, T_{1,1}, SL(2,Z) and the exact sequences with S_4 → S_3.
errors: No mathematical error. The claim that the tetrahedral barycentric subdivision 'contains' the square subdivisions holds only as a subdivision/embedding of graphs: some square edges are 2-edge paths through tetrahedral face centres. It is not a subcomplex, since 16 triangles do not group from 24 compatibly. Grothendieck's quotation marks around 'contenues' suggest he was aware of this.
The bottom pencil figure is unfinished and carries no stated claim.

ideas.what: Using the symmetric configurations (regular tetrahedron = equianharmonic, square = harmonic) together with degenerate pants configurations as base points for the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4}/S_4 ≅ M_{1,1}
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold points and tangential base points of the modular curve; Lego-Teichmüller tower at level (0,4)/(1,1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); developed by Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps, building on Moore–Seiberg-type presentations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2-3 (Teichmüller tower, base points, M_{0,4} and M_{1,1} as building blocks); the explicit tetrahedron/square visualisation is not there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Deforming the square configuration into the two tetrahedral ones by moving alternate vertices up or down; the two tetrahedra together form the cube
ideas.modern_name: Paths between orbifold points of orders 2 and 3 in M_{0,4}/S_4 (edge of the (2,3,∞) triangle); D_4 and A_4 inside the octahedral group S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein's polyhedral groups); its use as a Lego path is implicit in Grothendieck's program

ideas.what: Neighbouring base points of a special configuration are encoded by cells (edge midpoints, face centres) of the barycentric subdivision of the associated spherical map
ideas.modern_name: Dessins d'enfants / barycentric subdivision as a (2,3,n)-triangulation; flag complex of a map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (dessins, Esquisse); Malle–Matzat, Jones–Singerman on maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses maps and barycentric subdivision in general, not this specific statement

ideas.what: The barycentric subdivision of the tetrahedral map contains (as a subdivision) those of the three square maps, one per partition of the 4 points into 2 pairs
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the (2,3,3) and (2,2,4) spherical tessellations; both are coarsenings of the (2,3,4) octahedral tessellation

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a programme to visualise every elementary Lego path in M_{0,4}/S_4, conformally and combinatorially, through barycentric subdivisions of the special maps. The pantalonesque passage is only announced ('il faut introduire la subdivision barycentrique complète'), and the bottom figure is unfinished. Using the orbifold points themselves, not only tangential base points at infinity, as base points of the Teichmüller groupoid is a variant the later Lego literature largely did not pursue. That literature mostly works with tangential base points at infinity.
missed.quote: dans les deux cas "spéciaux" non dégénérés (carré, tétraèdre) les positions adjacentes sont toutes "contenues" dans la subdivision barycentrique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly relevant to explicit presentations of the profinite or GT-actions on π_1 of M_{0,4}/S_4 using orbifold-point base points. However, these are equivalent to standard treatments of SL(2,Z) ≅ Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6, so novelty is small.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear visual working note within the known Lego-Teichmüller programme for M_{0,4}. It contains elegant but classical geometry (square ↔ two tetrahedra ↔ cube; compatible barycentric subdivisions) and no result absent from the literature in substance.
transcription_corrections: Top right: 'passage du cube aux deux tétraèdres' is probably 'passage du carré aux deux tétraèdres'. The figure shows 4 points on the equator in square position, and p.17's 'cavrée' is likewise 'carrée'. Likewise 'de la carte cube' should read 'de la carte carré', and 'cartes "cubes" associées' should read 'cartes "carrés" associées'.
Right margin: 'aux structures pentagonales' should read 'aux structures pantalonesques'.
'Une carte (subdivision bar. des tétraèdres)' probably reads 'cette carte (subdivision bar. du tétraèdre)', with an overline/insertion above 'tétraèdre'.
'dont l'une est marquée en pointillés rouges' matches the red dotted lines in the middle figure.
